title: Italian City-States
capsule: The 'Italian City-States' polity for 91–87 BC represents the allied Italian communities (socii Italici) that revolted against Rome in the Social War, demanding citizenship and forming a rival confederate state with its capital at Corfinium, renamed Italica, minting their own coinage bearing the Italian bull goring the Roman wolf. The insurgents — Samnites, Marsi, Paeligni, Picentes, and others — fielded an army of approximately 100,000 and inflicted severe early Roman losses in 90 BC under consuls including Lucius Julius Caesar. Rome progressively neutralized the rebellion by extending citizenship to loyal communities through the lex Iulia of 90 BC and the lex Plautia Papiria of 89 BC, dissolving the confederate state by 87 BC as the surviving leaders fled or were captured.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The confederate state's territory — the homelands of the allied Italian peoples — is documented through Appian, Velleius Paterculus, and coinage; mapping it as a unified polity abstracts a loose military coalition whose members had varying levels of commitment and control.
